channel.title: The Coin Wire
channel.description: Crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation and protocol upgrades: what changed, and what comes next.

item.title: Convert Yield Tokens Before Bridging: What to Check
item.description: Converting a yield token to a bridge-supported asset can simplify a transfer, but fees, lost yield and destination liquidity determine whether it is worth doing.

item.title: How to Diagnose Direct and Multi-Hop Mantle Routes
item.description: Trace a Mantle route by separating its source transaction, bridge message and destination action; each stage points to a different cause when funds stall.

item.title: Two explorers show what a bridge quote leaves out
item.description: A bridge quote is an estimate; two chain explorers show the source fee actually paid on-chain and whether a separate destination transaction completed.

item.title: Why Wallet Bridge Transfers Take Longer Than a Swap
item.description: Bridge transfers take longer because the source chain must confirm a transaction and the destination chain must complete another; wallets often wait for both.

item.title: A confirmation is not the same as cross-chain finality
item.description: Confirmations show that a transaction is gaining support; finality sets a stronger settlement point, and cross-chain swaps must account for both chains and the route between them.

item.title: Moving USDC Between Chains: Choose the Route, Not Just the Fee
item.description: The cheapest quote may leave you with a different USDC version or less on arrival. Compare route mechanics, finality, liquidity and destination support before swapping.

item.title: Why a confirmed crypto transfer can still be stuck
item.description: A source-chain confirmation does not guarantee arrival: bridge relayers, proofs, liquidity and destination execution each add separate steps and failure modes.

item.title: Cross-chain payouts need a destination minimum
item.description: Cross-chain payouts can set a destination minimum instead of guessing the final balance, but fees, route failure and exact-output needs change the right choice.

item.title: Why Wallet Bridges Wait for More Confirmations
item.description: Wallet bridges wait for source-chain confirmations to reduce reorg risk, but thresholds vary by chain, bridge design and the speed or liquidity a route can offer.

item.title: A Confirmed Cross-Chain Swap Has Only Cleared Its First Test
item.description: A confirmed source transaction proves the first leg landed, not that the destination swap finished; check route status, recipient, and refund path before retrying.

item.title: Solana schedules Alpenglow for Oct. 21, targeting 150ms finality
item.description: Solana has scheduled Alpenglow for Oct. 21, replacing TowerBFT with a new voting system that targets 150ms finality but still depends on stake response.

item.title: DriveWealth adds RLUSD settlement in Europe, eyes US expansion
item.description: DriveWealth will use RLUSD on the XRP Ledger for European settlement and cross-border funding, adding a stablecoin route ahead of a planned US expansion.

item.title: Cross-Chain Swap Timing Depends on More Than Bridge Speed
item.description: Cross-chain swaps take longer than a normal trade because source-chain settlement, message delivery and destination execution happen in sequence; compare routes by each wait.

item.title: Cross-Chain Debt Repayment Starts Where the Loan Lives
item.description: Repaying debt across chains means moving the repayment asset to the chain where the loan lives, then settling it there; route, fees and timing shape the path.

item.title: Sui’s Hashi targets October launch with $500M committed
item.description: Sui says Hashi will roll out on mainnet this month with more than $500 million committed, backing BTC collateral markets while leaving deployment and security to prove out.

item.title: Injective puts fixed gas proposal to a live governance vote
item.description: Injective’s Proposal 709 would assign fixed gas to selected exchange messages; the vote is live, and mainnet adoption still depends on governance approval.

item.title: Manta Bridge transfers and swaps: where the extra step matters
item.description: A manta bridge transfer moves an asset between chains; adding a swap can combine routing and conversion, but changes what users must verify before signing.

item.title: How paraswap changes the bridge-and-swap decision
item.description: ParaSwap combines a cross-chain move and token swap in one flow; the practical choice depends on the route, destination asset, fees and bridge assumptions.

item.title: Ripple and Privy add embedded wallets to the XRP Ledger
item.description: Ripple and Stripe-owned Privy are adding XRPL wallets to Privy’s developer platform, letting apps support XRP and RLUSD without building wallet infrastructure.

item.title: XRP Ledger defends bypass of its amendment process for emergency patch
item.description: XRPL developers defended the Sept. 25 direct patch for an XRP-minting overflow, arguing the normal vote would have left the flaw exposed during weeks of upgrades.
